newsitem.title: ITALY: Theologians find bleeding Madonna a miracle - report.
newsitem.headline: Theologians find bleeding Madonna a miracle - report.

text.p: Theological experts investigating whether a statue of the Madonna wept blood have concluded that the event, which sparked miracle mania in Italy, was "supernatural", a newspaper said on Thursday.

"Miracle in Civitavecchia" ran the headline in Il Messaggero in an article about the reported conclusions of a commission of theologians and experts that studied the statue in the port town north of Rome.
The commission concluded after 14 meetings and some 50 eyewitness accounts that the white plaster statue had indeed shed tears of blood, the paper said.
The paper said the commission's conclusions, which will be sent to the Vatican's doctrinal department for review, had given "overall support" to the thesis of a miracle.
The Vatican, traditionally sceptical about claims of miracles, had no immediate comment on the report.
Archbishop Girolamo Grillo, who claims to have seen the statue bleed tears as he held it, declined to comment when contacted by phone, saying he now had to study the commission's 500-page conclusion.
"It's never good to rush into things," he said.
The 40-cm (15 inch) high statue of the virgin became an object of veneration for thousands of pilgrims in 1995 after the reported miracle sightings in Civitavecchia.
Initial scientific tests revealed that the red liquid streaking the statue's cheeks was male blood but there has been no conclusive explanation as to how it got there.
A local magistrate ordered church authorities to keep the statue temporarily under what the Italian media called "house arrest" last year pending an investigation into whether it was a hoax.

The statue was bought in the town of Medjugorje in Bosnia, a magnet for pligrims following reported apparitions of the Virgin there. Italy's constitutional court ruled last July that no DNA genetic testing should be carried out to determine the source of the blood.
